responsibility: This module is GCC’s target port for Atmel/Microchip AVR 8-bit microcontrollers, covering the full target-specific path from option and device selection through instruction selection, late RTL optimization, and driver/linker configuration. Its core backend files (`avr.cc`/`avr.h`) implement AVR target hooks for ABI details, register usage, calling conventions, prologue/epilogue generation, address spaces for RAM/flash/MEMX, builtin handling, costing, assembly emission, and machine-dependent lowering, while the machine-description family (`avr.md`, `constraints.md`, `predicates.md`, `avr-fixed.md`, `avr-dimode.md`, `avr-modes.def`) defines AVR instruction patterns, operand classes, fixed-point and wide-mode support, and nonstandard mode properties needed on an 8-bit architecture. The module also contains AVR-specific frontend and user-visible integration such as predefined macros, builtins, `<stdint.h>`/`<stdfix.h>` support, and diagnostics; target-specific RTL passes (`avr-passes.*`) for post-generic cleanup and code-quality improvements; and the canonical MCU/architecture database (`avr-arch.h`, `avr-devices.cc`, `avr-mcus.def`) that drives `-mmcu` interpretation, multilib selection, documentation generation, and per-device specs. Companion driver/spec files and generators (`driver-avr.cc`, `specs.h`, `avrlibc.h`, `gen-avr-mmcu-specs.cc`, `genmultilib.awk`, `gen-avr-mmcu-texi.cc`) distinguish this module from generic GCC code by encoding AVR device families, library/runtime startup choices, and multilib/doc support tied to concrete microcontrollers.
